paper.title_en: Effect of a single- \(\Lambda\) impurity on the magnetic response of finite nuclei
paper.abstract_en:
$\textbf{Background:}$ Ultrastrong magnetic fields, which can be generated transiently in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, can significantly modify the structure of finite nuclei. However, how a single-\(\Lambda\) impurity embedded in a nuclear core alters the magnetic response of finite nuclei remains unclear.$\textbf{Purpose:}$ To investigate the effect of a single-\(\Lambda\) impurity on the magnetic response of finite nuclei, focusing on separation energies, single-particle levels, deformation, radii, and density distributions.
$\textbf{Method:}$ A nonrelativistic three-dimensional Skyrme-Hartree-Fock approach was employed with self-consistent coupling to an external magnetic field. The \(\text{SLy}4 +\text{SLL}4\) interaction combination was used for the main calculations, and additional \(\text{SLy}5 + \text{SLL}4\) and \(\text{SLy}4 +\text{LY}1\) results were included to assess the interaction dependence.
$\textbf{Results:}$ The calculations were performed for \({}_{\Lambda}^{17}\text{O}\), \({}_{\Lambda}^{29}\text{Si}\), and \({}_{\Lambda}^{41}\text{Ca}\), together with their cores, under ultrastrong magnetic fields. We analyze the effects of the \(\Lambda\) impurity on the core radii, deformation, single-particle spectra, and density distributions, as well as the magnetic field dependence of the \(\Lambda\) separation energy, root-mean-square (rms) radius, and density distribution. Under strong magnetic fields, the \(\Lambda\) impurity shrinks the nucleonic density distribution, reduces the core radii, weakens the deformation response, and modifies the level-rearrangement pattern of the nuclear core.
$\textbf{Conclusions´:}$ The single-\(\Lambda\) impurity modifies the core magnetic response via the attractive \(\Lambda N\) interaction and nucleonic rearrangement, while its direct magnetic coupling mainly affects the \(\Lambda\) single-particle energy.
